title: The hooks
subtitle: One turn in Claude Code, and which hook steps in when.

phases.label: The tool call
phases.blurb: Bash, Edit or Write runs here

chips.label: usage-guard prompt
chips.what: Starts a refresh of the usage meter and, when the usage alarm is up, adds a note to the prompt.
how: It runs on UserPromptSubmit and starts a detached `lighthouse usage refresh`.
With an alarm it adds a note as additionalContext; it never blocks.
The alarm is one line in ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/lighthouse/usage-window.alarm, written by the usage meter; the guard never removes it.
It always exits 0; when it cannot check, it says so on stderr.
chips.without: The session runs into the limit without a warning, and the meter is not refreshed.

chips.label: worktree-guard
chips.what: Warns, and never blocks, at a write into the main checkout on main.
how: It checks the target file path of the Edit or Write, not the working directory.
It compares the git dir with the common git dir to tell a linked worktree from the main checkout, and reads the protected branch from lighthouse.toml.
On a match it returns a systemMessage with the git worktree add command; when it cannot check, the message says COULD NOT CHECK.
It always exits 0.
chips.without: A write into the main checkout on main passes without a warning.

chips.label: main-commit-guard
chips.what: Blocks git commit and git push on the default branch.
how: It reads the default branch from `forge.default_branch` in lighthouse.toml, and uses main when it is not set.
It also sees a commit after `cd` and through `git -C <path>`.
A commit or push there blocks with exit 2 and a message on stderr. `touch .claude/allow-main` in the repo root is the deliberate escape hatch.
When it cannot see where a commit goes, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.without: A commit or push lands directly on main.

chips.label: commit-tests pre
chips.what: Blocks a commit with --no-verify and tests a commit to the default branch before it happens.
how: It sees a commit after `cd`, `;`, `|`, `&&` or with `git -C <path>`, and tests the tree that is committed.
For a commit to the default branch it runs the test gate up front; red blocks with exit 2.
For every other commit it records the HEAD before the commit, so `post` knows what the commit touched.
When it cannot parse the command or resolve the tree, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.without: A commit skips the gate with --no-verify, and a commit to main goes in untested.

chips.label: pr-create-gate
chips.what: Blocks a gh pr create whose body has no evidence.
how: It checks the body of the `gh pr create` call.
The body must hold `Closes #N` with an Evidence table, `Refs #N — <reason>` or `No issue: <reason>`.
Otherwise it blocks with exit 2 and a message on stderr; the check is in lighthouse_lib/pr_body_gate.py.
When it cannot check, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.when: Before each Bash call that runs gh pr create.
chips.without: A PR opens without a Closes line and evidence.

chips.label: bash-write-gates pre
chips.what: Records a baseline of the files before a Bash call, so post can see what the call wrote.
how: It is a thin wrapper around lighthouse_lib/bash_writes.py.
It records the baseline and a marker, and always exits 0: a PreToolUse exit 2 would block the Bash call itself.
It stays silent by design; post reports a failure loudly.
chips.without: The post gate cannot tell which files a Bash call wrote.

chips.label: worktree-linkcheck
chips.what: Blocks a markdown link that is absolute or points nowhere.
how: It checks only .md and .markdown files.
It finds the git root of the written file, and md_links.py resolves each relative link against the directory of that file.
A dead or absolute link blocks with exit 2 and a list of the bad targets.
When jq, git or python3 is missing, or the parser fails, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.without: A broken or absolute link in a .md file is committed.

chips.label: code-language
chips.what: Blocks code whose names, comments or docstrings are not in English.
how: It is on only with `[project] code_language` in the lighthouse.toml of the git root of the written file.
It always reads .py, .sh, .bash and .go files; anything else only inside `[project] code_language_paths`.
A finding blocks with exit 2 and stderr; a line marked `lighthouse: allow-language` is skipped.
When the optional model check gives no verdict, it prints a notice without a judgment and does not block; when it cannot check at all, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.without: Dutch comments, docstrings and names land in code that must be English.

chips.label: commit-tests post
chips.what: Tests what a commit touched with the test gate, and reports red.
how: Per recorded root whose HEAD moved, it runs `[test_gate] command` from lighthouse.toml with the changed files in LIGHTHOUSE_GATE_FILES.
Red is exit 2 after the commit: the commit stays and the fix comes in a new commit.
Without a command the commit passes with a note that nothing was tested.
When it cannot parse the command or resolve the tree, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.when: After each Bash call, also one that failed.
chips.without: A commit with red tests goes unnoticed.

chips.label: gofmt
chips.what: Runs gofmt -w on an edited Go file.
how: Formatting is silent and does not block.
A file that does not parse blocks with exit 2: gofmt cannot format it, and every later check would run on broken code.
Without jq or gofmt, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
A file with another extension, or none, leaves nothing to check.
chips.without: Go files are left unformatted, and a file that does not parse goes unnoticed.

chips.label: bash-write-gates post
chips.what: Runs the Edit and Write gates on the files a Bash call wrote.
how: It compares against the baseline of pre and sends each dirty file through its gate: shellcheck, ruff-format, code-language for .py, .sh, .bash and .go files, and worktree-linkcheck.
A finding blocks with exit 2.
A gate whose package is not installed is reported per file, without blocking.
When it cannot check, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
chips.when: After each Bash call, also one that failed.
chips.without: What a Bash call writes skips the gates that an Edit or Write passes.

chips.label: ruff-format
chips.what: Runs ruff format and ruff check --fix on an edited Python file.
how: Pass 1 formats and fixes, silently and without blocking.
Pass 2 blocks with exit 2 on eight rules (BLOCKING_RULES in the script) that are kept at zero across the repo.
Without jq, uvx or ruff, or with a ruff that does not start, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK.
A file with another extension, or none, leaves nothing to check.
chips.without: Python files are left unformatted, and a blocking ruff rule goes unnoticed.

chips.label: shellcheck
chips.what: Runs shellcheck on an edited shell script.
how: In the directories of `shell.strict_dirs` (default `.claude/hooks`) every finding blocks, down to style.
In every other .sh file only errors and warnings block.
A finding blocks with exit 2.
When shellcheck or the tooling is missing, it blocks with COULD NOT CHECK; it is never silent.
chips.without: A shell script with a shellcheck finding is committed.

chips.label: usage-guard tool
chips.what: With the usage alarm up, blocks once per window so the session wraps up.
how: It runs after every tool call; without an alarm the cost is one file test.
The alarm is one line in ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/lighthouse/usage-window.alarm, written by the usage meter; the guard never removes it.
With an alarm it blocks once per window with `{"decision": "block"}` and exit 0, not exit 2.
In a controller run it also writes the pause flag. It is fail-open: when it cannot check, it says so on stderr.
chips.without: The session runs into the limit instead of wrapping up.

chips.label: usage-guard subagent
chips.what: With the usage alarm up, blocks once per subagent so it wraps up.
how: It runs when a subagent stops.
The alarm is one line in ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/lighthouse/usage-window.alarm, written by the usage meter; the guard never removes it.
With an alarm it blocks once per subagent with `{"decision": "block"}` and exit 0, not exit 2.
It is fail-open: when it cannot check, it says so on stderr.
chips.without: A subagent runs into the limit instead of wrapping up.

chips.label: go-check
chips.what: Runs golangci-lint at the end of a turn that touched Go.
how: It lints only a checkout in which the turn touched a Go path: an edit, a Bash write or a commit; the rest gets `not checked`.
A finding, or a build that fails, blocks with exit 2 and sends the findings back to the model.
While the usage alarm is up, it says `not checked` and exits 0.
When it cannot check, it exits 0 with a systemMessage `go-check: COULD NOT CHECK`, since blocking there would keep the session from stopping.
chips.when: At the end of each turn.
chips.without: Lint findings in Go code are left for the next turn.

chips.label: ty-check
chips.what: Runs ty check on the Python source directories at the end of a turn that touched Python.
how: It checks the directories in `python.source_dirs`, and only a checkout in which the turn touched a .py or .pyi file there, pyproject.toml, ty.toml or uv.lock.
A diagnostic blocks with exit 2 and sends it back to the model.
While the usage alarm is up, it says `not checked` and exits 0; `python.source_dirs = []` turns it off.
When it cannot check, it exits 0 with a systemMessage `ty-check: COULD NOT CHECK`.
chips.when: At the end of each turn.
chips.without: Type errors in Python code are left for the next turn.

chips.label: usage-guard stop
chips.what: With the usage alarm up, blocks once per window at the end of a turn so the session wraps up.
how: It runs on Stop.
The alarm is one line in ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/lighthouse/usage-window.alarm, written by the usage meter; the guard never removes it.
With an alarm it blocks once per window with `{"decision": "block"}` and exit 0, not exit 2.
It is fail-open: when it cannot check, it says so on stderr.
chips.when: At the end of each turn.
chips.without: The session ends without wrapping up, and the next one runs into the limit.
